rationale: The stated rationale is algebraically wrong — with a and b the two industry ranks, the "long corner" is (1−a)b and the "short corner" is a(1−b), whose difference is exactly b−a, so this construction collapses almost entirely into the linear rank difference it claims to avoid and is a repackaging of two archive signals rather than new information.

The expression matches the hypothesis and the profitability-record conjunct is economically distinct from turnover trend, but it is an incremental extension of the archive's best long signal and the discrete five-year loss counter will inject heavy ties even after industry ranking, so the marginal payoff is modest.

The sign is backwards relative to both the accrual anomaly (an increase in payables *reduces* accruals and predicts higher returns) and the archive's own payables test, whose wrong-signed FMB slope (+1.07 against a negative prior) already indicates payables stretching is not a negative-return state, so penalizing payables growth on the long side lacks support.

Internally consistent and reasonably motivated by the asymmetry argument for why the cash channel should work on the long side, though both legs lean on well-known ingredients (gross profitability trend, cash holdings) and Δcash/sales is badly confounded by financing flows even in the top corner.

A legitimate, internally consistent repair of the tie-laden loss-frequency conditioner with a continuous worst-case ROA and uniform industry ranking, but it will be highly correlated with the existing archive version, so it should be judged on incremental improvement rather than treated as a new mechanism.

The sign convention on `invch` is handled correctly and the corner is not a mechanical flip of the archive's obsolescence signal, but low inventory growth relative to sales/COGS growth is a long-established published anomaly (Abarbanell–Bushee inventory signal; Thomas–Zhang inventory growth), making this largely a rediscovery dressed as a diagnostic.
